outcomes.text: Define history as a discipline, its subject matter and scope.
Tell the branches of history apart.
Tell approaches apart, e.g. Marxist, Subaltern, Feminist, Orientalist, National, military, social-cultural and oral history.
Identify causation as the driving force of historical change.
Understand periodization and the different ways history is divided into periods.
Identify the geography and features of Arabia before Islam.
Evaluate the tribal politics of Arabia and its major tribes.
Link Arabia's geography and climate to its society, culture and way of life.
Understand the Kaabah's central place in Meccan society and Arab religion.
Trace the Prophet's life from birth to the call to prophethood at forty.
Analyse why Quraish rejected Islam in Mecca's mixed religious setting.
Chronicle the main events of the 13 Makkan years until the migration.
Evaluate why Yathrib was chosen as the base of the Islamic state.
Inspect the first tasks in Madina: the mosque, refugees and the Charter of Madina.
Summarize the conflicts with Quraish and the shift of power they caused.
Examine relations with the Jews of Madina and Khyber and why disputes arose and ended.
Explain why the Treaty of Hudaibiya mattered for peace with Quraish.
Outline the Prophet's covenant with the Christians of Mt. Sinai and its value for Muslim-Christian relations.
Describe the events leading to the Conquest of Mecca.
Stress the Farewell Pilgrimage and Last Sermon for Islam's social values and moral code.
Recognise the Prophet as teacher, statesman and strategist who changed Arabia in every way.
Deconstruct the need to unite the ummah and the Apostasy Wars under Abu Bakr.
Review the fast expansion and the administration set up by Umar.
Outline the problems arising in the Muslim community under Uthman.
Evaluate the rise of factions and the Khawarij under Ali.
Identify the shift to Banu Umayyah, hereditary rule under Muawiya and Yazid, and Karbala.
Analyse the Arab character given to the state by Abdul Malik bin Marwan.
Assess consolidation and expansion under Waleed bin Abdul Malik.
Deconstruct why Umayyad rule grew unpopular and how Umar bin Abdul Aziz and Hisham tried to reconcile.
Outline the Abbasid Revolution and its success under Marwan the Second.
Explain the concept of the Caliphate.
Categorize the state and administrative system of the Umayyads.
Outline the Umayyads' economic system.
Explain Umayyad social organization and the exclusively Arab culture.

topics.title: Society and culture of the Umayyads

outcomes.text: Explain Umayyad social organization and the exclusively Arab culture.
Outline the Umayyads' architectural contributions.
Analyse the Umayyad downfall, especially their treatment of non-Arab subjects.
List how Abbasid rule was consolidated under Saffah and Mansoor.
Appraise the growth of the Caliphate under Al Mahdi and Al Hadi.
Evaluate the Golden Age under Harun ur Rashid and al Ma'mun.
Discern Persian influence, the Zindeeq and the Barmakids' role in government.
Assess the results of growing Turkish influence meant to balance the Persians.
Outline how Abd al Rehman al Dakhil founded Umayyad rule in Iberia.
Analyse Abd al-Rahman III taking the title of Caliph and the Caliphate of Cordoba.
Tell the administrative and ethnic reasons for the Taifas.
Survey the Convivencia of peoples of many faiths.
Evaluate Cordoba's intellectual, cultural and architectural contributions.
Analyse why autonomous dynasties arose under Abbasid rule.
Evaluate the reasons for the Crusades and Muslim control of Palestine.
Describe events leading to the Mongol conquest and fall of Baghdad in 1258.
Analyse how the Caliphate changed in nature under the Abbasids.
Outline Abbasid administration: the Wazir, central and provincial diwans.
Categorize the Iqta system, Abbasid markets and growth in farming, industry and trade.
Outline the ethnic and language identities of Abbasid society.
Determine the status of women in the Abbasid court.
Appreciate religious diversity in Abbasid society.
Review Abbasid architecture.
Trace musicology in the Abbasid era and its key musicians.
Appreciate Abbasid art.
Evaluate the rise, beliefs and influence of Mu'tazilism.
Analyse the formation of the schools of jurisprudence (madhahib).
Trace the beginning of Sufi doctrine in Baghdad.
Trace the Translation Movement and the role of Bait ul Hikma.
Outline Abbasid advances in geography, history, geology, mathematics, astronomy, chemistry, biology and physics.
Analyse the influence of Abbasid science on the West.
Explain the education system described in Al Ghazali's work.
Analyse the political philosophy of al-Farabi.
Appreciate Ibn Sina's contributions to science and philosophy.
Expound the work of the polymath Ibn Rushd.
